ch-verses-p1.englishMeaning: Overcome anger through non-anger; overcome wickedness through goodness; overcome miserliness through generosity; and overcome falsehood through truth.
ch-verses-p1.expanded_english: When another person approaches in anger, one should remain calm and retain rational judgement rather than responding with anger. Dishonest conduct should be defeated through greater honesty, miserliness through generosity, and falsehood through strict truthfulness. The verse teaches the strategy of overcoming a negative tendency by cultivating its opposite positive quality.
ch-verses-p1.hindiMeaning: क्रोध को अक्रोध और शान्ति से, दुष्टता को सदाचार से, कृपणता को दान से और असत्य को सत्य से जीतना चाहिए।
ch-verses-p1.expanded_hindi: जब कोई व्यक्ति क्रोध में आकर सामना करे, तब स्वयं क्रोधित होने के बजाय मन को शान्त और विवेकपूर्ण रखना चाहिए। बेईमानी का सामना अधिक ईमानदारी से, कृपणता का उदार दान से और झूठ का कठोर सत्यनिष्ठा से करना चाहिए। यह पद नकारात्मक प्रवृत्ति को उसके विपरीत सकारात्मक गुण द्वारा जीतने की नीति सिखाता है।

ch-verses-p1.editorial_note: The AMPS discourse preserves a transliterated Pāli verse and supplies practical explanation. Canonical English/Hindi drafts may be derived from that discourse explanation. The original verse is Dhammapada 223 (Kodhavagga). Exact AMPS printed Devanagari and Roman remain preserved in provenance; standard Pāli reading is stored under Original Source Reference.
ch-verses-p1.source_evidence: The cited AMPS discourse quotes the verse and explains its clauses (non-anger, honesty/goodness, generosity, truth). Compact translation variants appear across AMPS materials. Complete wording matches Dhammapada 223 in the Pāli Canon. AMPS printed form preserved separately.

Akkodhena jine kodhaṁ,

jine kadariyaṁ dānena,
saccenālikavādinaṁ.

textual_comparison.difference_note: The AMPS form is a Devanagari and Roman transcription of the Pāli verse. Differences mainly concern spelling, vowel length, word division and transliteration. Exact AMPS printed form preserved unchanged in provenance.

ch-verses-p3.englishMeaning: He is inconceivable, unmanifest and of infinite forms; auspicious, supremely peaceful, immortal and the source of Brahma. He is the one all-pervading Consciousness-Bliss, wondrous and without beginning, middle or end.
ch-verses-p3.expanded_english: The Supreme is beyond imagination and sense perception, yet manifests through countless forms. He is auspicious, supremely peaceful, immortal, the source of all creation, and the one all-pervading embodiment of Consciousness and Bliss, without beginning, middle or end.
ch-verses-p3.hindiMeaning: वह परम सत्ता चिन्तन से परे, अव्यक्त और अनन्त रूपों वाली है। वह कल्याणमय, परम शान्त, अमर, ब्रह्म की मूल योनि तथा आदि, मध्य और अन्त से रहित एकमात्र सर्वव्यापी चैतन्य और आनन्दस्वरूप अद्भुत सत्ता है।

ch-verses-p3.source_evidence: Subháśita Saḿgraha Part 2, The Intuitional Science of the Vedas – 4, explains the verse clause-by-clause across following paragraphs (unimaginable/unmanifest, Shiva/benevolent, Brahma, beginningless, Consciousness-Bliss, formless/wondrous). No bracketed translation immediately after the verse. Concise meaning is a source-derived summary, not a direct quotation.
